bull.b: Rapidly rising AUCATZYL revenue and higher full-year guidance indicate strengthening commercial adoption and expanding demand. If this trajectory continues, increasing product scale can improve operating leverage, support reinvestment in the pipeline, and establish a more durable recurring revenue base.

The sharp gross-margin improvement shows that production economics are becoming more favorable as volumes increase and cost-reduction initiatives take effect. Reaching the stated mature margin target would materially strengthen cash generation potential and reduce the funding burden of commercial expansion.

A broader authorized-center network expands patient access and creates more capacity for AUCATZYL administration. Continued geographic and site expansion can support durable commercial growth by improving reach, strengthening the treatment infrastructure, and increasing the addressable flow of eligible patients.

bear.b: Large recurring cash outflows and continued net losses mean the company has not yet achieved self-funding operations. Unless revenue growth and margins improve materially, ongoing burn could require additional financing and limit flexibility to invest in development, commercialization, or other strategic priorities.

A substantial portion of planned financing is conditional on future commercial performance rather than fully committed capital. If revenue milestones are delayed or missed, available liquidity could be lower than expected, increasing execution pressure and potentially forcing less favorable funding or spending decisions.

The company is carrying a significant cost base while scaling commercialization and advancing multiple clinical programs. Higher SG&A and sustained R&D spending can delay breakeven, absorb the benefit of revenue growth, and keep operating leverage uncertain until sales scale sufficiently.
